title: Cells 1+3 methodology replication: 5-stage manual + Z-gate generalization test

r_precision_at_k_methodology_note.definition: R-Precision@K = (1/Q) * sum_{q in Q} r_q / min(K, R_q), per [[project-r-precision-methodology]]. Tie-break (p_calibrated desc, ticker asc) stable mergesort; macro-averaged across days with R_q > 0.

headline: Methodology FAILS on both cells (0 of 2 PASS the test-R-p@1 >= sweep floor). Cell-1 manual winner test R-p@1=0.6600 vs sweep 0.800 (FAIL, -0.140 absolute, 82.5% of sweep). Cell-3 manual winner test R-p@1=0.4267 vs sweep 0.600 (FAIL, -0.173 absolute, 71.1% of sweep). Z-gate finding from _223 (mcw -> |z| -> calibration decision -> R-p@1) does NOT generalize: minimum val |z| achievable on cells 1+3 across 80+ configs was 12.04 (cell-3 spw=4.0) / 18.84 (cell-1 d=3+cs=0.3+mcw=1+FS=100) — an order of magnitude above the |z|=2 isotonic-gate threshold. Calibration always fires isotonic on these strong-AUC cells. Methodology rule 11 (5-stage manual) is best framed as a fallback when the loop's val_brier objective is misaligned (rule 10), NOT as a general-purpose improvement engine.

z_gate_generalization.claim_being_tested: Per _223: min_child_weight controls val Spiegelhalter |z|, which determines conditional_isotonic's decision (native vs isotonic), which determines how many distinct calibrated predictions survive into test, which determines R-p@1. On cell-5, mcw=5 -> |z|=1.56 < 2 -> native -> 225 distinct cal preds -> R-p@1=0.7143.
z_gate_generalization.cell3_min_z_config: spw=4.0 (eval R-p@1 dropped to 0.317, actively hurt the operating metric)
z_gate_generalization.mechanism: The booster on a strong-AUC cell (cell-1 AUC=0.903, cell-3 AUC=0.776) generates highly confident predictions far from the base rate; the Spiegelhalter z-statistic is structurally large regardless of HP. mcw cannot push |z| below 12 on either cell. Conditional_isotonic ALWAYS fires; the mcw axis has no leverage on the calibration decision.

methodology_5_stage_generalization.claim_being_tested: Per _211: FS cliff cut -> single-knob response curves -> mix-and-match -> eval validation -> 1-shot test shootout. Beats sweep R-p@1 by +24% on cell-5.
methodology_5_stage_generalization.best_relative_to_sweep: cell-1: 82.5% of sweep R-p@1 (gap -0.140); cell-3: 71.1% of sweep R-p@1 (gap -0.173).
methodology_5_stage_generalization.best_relative_to_un_tuned_XGBoost_defaul: cell-1: +0.120 over baseline; cell-3: +0.213 over baseline.
methodology_5_stage_generalization.interpretation: The methodology recovers SOME signal vs un-tuned XGBoost defaults on both cells, but cannot close the XGBoost-vs-CatBoost backend gap. CatBoost sweep dominates the XGBoost-manual configuration space tested.
methodology_5_stage_generalization.playbook_amendment_proposed: Rule 11 should state: 'this methodology applies when the loop val_brier objective is misaligned (rule 10) -- that is, the iter_0 anti_auc_flag is true.' On strong-AUC cells the methodology has no leverage over the sweep baseline.

fs.rank_basis: iter_0 XGBoost feature_importance (gain), pruned floor at importance < 0.01

stage_summary.stage4_best_eval_rp1: skipped — top-3 mix stayed in pool

eval_test_oracle_failure.interpretation: Eval R-p@1 was an unreliable oracle on cell-3. The methodology's stage-4-eval-validation step (rank by eval R-p@1) would have committed to sub=0.7 as the test pick; the actual test winner was rank 6 by eval. This is a stronger failure of the methodology than the headline 'FAIL on R-p@1 >= sweep' verdict: even the methodology's INTERNAL stages 4-5 ordering does not reliably surface the test winner.

cross_cell_synthesis.no_universal_recipe_reconfirmed: The cell-5 winning config (XGBoost depth-2 + cs=0.4 + mcw=5 + FS=top-130 + eta=0.1+ES=30, the 'cell5_template' in stage 3) was tested on both cells: cell-1 eval R-p@1=0.160, cell-3 eval R-p@1=0.293 -- neither close to top-3 mix winners. The cell-5 cell-specific config does NOT carry over to cells 1+3. Confirms playbook rule 8 ('no transferable recipe across cell shapes').
cross_cell_synthesis.xgboost_vs_catboost_gap_codified: On both cells, XGBoost-manual best is well below CatBoost sweep on R-p@1 despite essentially matching test AUC (cell-1 manual AUC=0.913 vs sweep 0.903; cell-3 manual AUC=0.756 vs sweep 0.775). The gap is concentrated in the top-1 prediction-tail bucket, not in bulk ranking. Most likely mechanism: CatBoost's ordered boosting handles the panel-pooled walk-forward structure better than XGBoost's standard boosting on these specific cell shapes. Dedicated investigation out of scope for this task.
cross_cell_synthesis.v1_3_b_relevance_revised: V1.3 Option B (#213, scout response-curve phase) is no longer load-bearing for closing cell-5's 0.115 gap to the manual track (per _223 conclusion), and the cells 1+3 result here further reduces the cross-cell value: the agent loop's current envelope is enough to identify that strong-AUC cells are NOT Z-gate-controllable, and a scout response curve would just confirm |z| > 12 at iter_0. May still be useful for cells we haven't characterized yet.
